Engine Room Records • Official Imprint & Studio Gateway

“What Kind of Music Do I Make?”

Welcome to Engine Room Records (engineroom.raggiesoft.com, also reachable via our vanity domain engineroom-records.com). In real life, Engine Room Records is the private creative imprint under which Michael P. Ragsdale writes, engineers, and distributes 38 albums (455 songs) across seven distinct musical projects—spanning 1980s stadium synth-rock, zero-gravity 80s Cosmic Pop, British art-rock operas, holiday symphonic metal, 16-bit RPG progressive rock, and 1980s fantasy-adventure movie soundtracks.

Core Pillar 01 • Roster & Genre Directory

1. What Kind of Music Do I Make? (The 7 Projects)

Rather than forcing every genre under a single artist name, each musical style and narrative universe has its own dedicated band project. Select any project below to stream full tracks, read synchronized lyrics, or download free CC BY-SA 4.0 128kbps MP3 archives in The Listening Room.

ERR-001 20 Releases • 254 Tracks

The Stardust Engine

80s Synth-Pop / Arena Rock / 80s Cosmic Pop

What It Sounds Like: High-energy 1980s stadium AOR, driving analog synthesizers, sibling vocal duets, progressive rock suites (including the 15-minute "Escape Velocity / Ad Astra"), and lush zero-gravity "80s Cosmic Pop."

The founding five-member family unit behind Engine Room Records. Forged at Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) in 1985–1986 by siblings Ryan, Cassidy, and Holly O'Connell and identical twin cousins Evan and Tyler Wright, The Stardust Engine blends soaring 1980s stadium synth-rock with Cassidy's zero-gravity Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™.

🎧 Listen in The Listening Room ↗ 🚀 Cosmic Portal (stardust.raggiesoft.com) ↗ 📚 Companion Book ↗
ERR-002 3 Releases • 14 Tracks

Fractured Prisms

80s Progressive Art-Rock / British Synth-Pop / Victorian Rock Opera

What It Sounds Like: Lush 1980s British progressive synth-pop, classical wooden concert flute lead melodies ("Gwen's Flute"), Roland/Yamaha analog sequencers and LinnDrum gated percussion, and cinematic Victorian-meets-1980s concept albums.

Formed by surviving British-American siblings Claire Manning (older sister; autistic and living with lifelong cerebral palsy, uses a manual wheelchair) and Rhys Manning (younger brother; neurotypical synthesizer architect and lifelong safe person) after the winter 1981 M6 Shap Fell motorway pileup claimed the other four members of the Manning Family Orchestra. Fleeing to their father's vacant 1960s ranch house in Williamsport, Maryland, they built "The Fragile Fortress"—weaving the salvaged instruments of their lost family (including Cousin Gwen's wooden concert flute) into towering 1980s analog synthesizer rock operas set inside the gaslamp-lit 1883 Victorian sanctuary of The Hollow Square.

🎧 Listen in The Listening Room ↗ 📖 Fractured Prisms Lore & Roster 📚 Companion Book ↗
ERR-003 5 Releases • 72 Tracks

The Paper Wall

Literary Rock Opera / Alternative & Industrial Rock

What It Sounds Like: Emotionally raw theatrical rock operas, dynamic quiet-to-loud alternative rock builds, industrial percussion, and autobiographical storytelling across multi-book concept albums.

Engine Room Records' first outside signing (2001). Formed by Julian Croft ("Leo") and Maya Sterling ("Olivia") alongside Julian's sisters and cousins, The Paper Wall transforms survival, disability rights, and found-family sanctuary into multi-volume literary rock operas.

🎧 Listen in The Listening Room ↗ 📖 The Paper Wall Lore & Roster 📚 Companion Book ↗
ERR-005 2 Releases • 32 Tracks

The Arctic Symphony Project

Holiday Symphonic Rock / Neoclassical Metal / Rock Opera

What It Sounds Like: Sweeping Trans-Siberian-scale symphonic rock, soaring distorted electric guitars, Baroque cello counter-melodies, silver glockenspiel, Brahms music-box motifs, and trilingual choirs (Cymraeg Welsh, Québécois French, and English).

Born on a freezing December night in 1996 when the Rowlands and Harrison siblings turned their Williamsburg living room into an emergency broadcast studio to guide abducted 14-year-old Julian ("Julep") home across the Appalachian Mountains with "Upon This Winter's Night."

🎧 Listen in The Listening Room ↗ 📖 The Arctic Symphony Project Lore & Roster 📚 Companion Book ↗
ERR-006 1 Releases • 15 Tracks

Crimson Node

Stadium Synth-Prog / 80s Arena Rock / Power-Pop

What It Sounds Like: High-octane stadium synth-prog, precision rhythm-section grooves ("Quality of Service", "The Flight Path"), and rotating four-part female lead vocals.

Engineered inside a sound-dampened Albemarle County garage by the Miller, Brooks, and Pelletier family phalanx, Crimson Node is directed by non-verbal wheelchair-using producer Matt Miller from his custom Tactile Command Rig and fronted by a powerhouse rotating vocal lineup.

🎧 Listen in The Listening Room ↗ 📖 Crimson Node Lore & Roster 📚 Companion Book ↗
ERR-004 2 Releases • 24 Tracks

Mana Canvas

Symphonic Fantasy Rock / 16-Bit Chiptune Prog / JRPG Soundtrack

What It Sounds Like: 16-bit SNES RPG chiptune leads fused with symphonic progressive rock, fantasy acoustic ballads, and live concert rock operas.

The official musical voice of the Runebreaker / Dream Kingdom universe. Mana Canvas fuses authentic 16-bit Super Famicom / SNES SPC-700 synth nostalgia with roaring progressive rock guitars, orchestral strings, and arena singalongs.

🎧 Listen in The Listening Room ↗ 📖 Mana Canvas Lore & Roster 📚 Companion Book ↗
ERR-007 4 Releases • 42 Tracks

Firelight

80s Movie Soundtracks / 80s Synth-Pop / Fantasy-Adventure Score

What It Sounds Like: 1980s fantasy-adventure movie soundtracks, shimmering Limahl-inspired 80s synth-pop title themes ("A Sister's Love"), power-rock villain and battle anthems, and sweeping orchestral film scores.

The official 1980s motion picture soundtrack ensemble behind The Silver Gauntlet of Aethel—Michael P. Ragsdale's love letter to 1980s fantasy-adventure cinema. Anchored by its flagship main theme "A Sister's Love" (heavily inspired by Limahl's iconic NeverEnding Story theme song), Firelight fuses shimmering 1980s analog synth-pop arpeggios and soaring melodic hooks with widescreen fantasy orchestration.

🎧 Listen in The Listening Room ↗ 📖 Firelight Lore & Roster 📚 Companion Book ↗
ERR-008 1 Releases • 2 Tracks

The Hoshizora Ensemble

70s Japanese Folk-Pop / City Pop / Maritime Easy Listening

What It Sounds Like: Breezy 1978 Japanese acoustic folk-pop and maritime City Pop featuring warm fingerpicked acoustic guitars, gentle electric bass, soft brushed percussion, and lush harmonic vocals in both original Japanese and the 2002 Engine Room Records English studio translation.

Originally recorded in Osaka in May 1978 as the official shipboard passenger cabin soundtrack for the overnight Ferry Hoshizora on Japan's Seto Inland Sea, The Hoshizora Ensemble's "Hoshizora no Uta: Voyages on the Seto Inland Sea" was licensed for North American distribution by Holly O'Connell in 2002 during the Japanese leg of The Stardust Engine's Midnight Drivers World Tour—an overnight ferry crossing that directly inspired the 2003 Twin Moons project.

Core Pillar 02 • Studio Transparency

2. Behind the Scenes on Music Generation

Full engineering transparency into how human direction, narrative libretto writing, acoustic & phonetic vowel extensions, and the 74% Cover Audio Influence protocol shape every release.

Human Direction + AI Studio Pipeline

Every song begins with Michael P. Ragsdale's human creative direction, narrative architecture, and co-written lyrics with Google Gemini, engineered into audio via a commercial Suno v5 / v6 studio subscription and mastered locally through our automated Harper Audio Engine.

Read Pipeline Spec →

Phonetic Vowel Extension & 74% Cover Protocol

To prevent clipped phrasing and unlock sustained stadium vocal belts, lyrics are engineered with explicit phonetic vowel extensions (ooh, aah, ee, oh). For our remastered Starfield Calibration sessions, a precise 74% Audio Influence Cover ratio preserved original melodies while upgrading acoustic separation.

Explore 74% Protocol →

The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ vs. 80s Cosmic Pop

We protect The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ as the proprietary brand mark of The Stardust Engine, while keeping the underlying genre descriptor—“80s Cosmic Pop”—100% open and free for any musician or creator to use.

View Open-Culture Policy →
Core Pillar 03 • Dual-Layer Architecture

3. The Corporate Entity of Engine Room Records

Understanding the boundary between our real-world publishing brand and our in-universe fictional conglomerate.

Real-World Reality (Non-Fiction)

Engine Room Records (Strictly NO “LLC”)

In the real world, there is only Engine Room Records—never Engine Room Records, LLC. It is the sole-proprietor creative brand and record imprint under which Michael P. Ragsdale publishes his music to Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, and The Listening Room.

  • Owner & Executive Producer: Michael P. Ragsdale
  • Consumer Free Downloads: 128kbps MP3 tracks & album ZIPs licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 on music.raggiesoft.com.
  • Commercial Sync Clearance: Direct B2B synchronization licensing via /commercial-licensing.
DSP Chain-of-Custody Ledger →
In-Universe Narrative Lore (Work of Fiction)

Engine Room Records, LLC & The O'Connell Family Trust

Anything with “LLC”, “Trust”, or “Holdings” in its name is strictly a fictitious, in-universe narrative entity. Within the story world, Engine Room Records, LLC was founded in 1992 by Holly O'Connell, J.D., CFA after The Stardust Engine walked out of Apex Records' Friction sessions.

  • Parent Trust: The O'Connell Family Revocable Trust (Est. 2012 / 2015 DE Restructure, $2.4B+ AUM).
  • Subsidiaries: The O'Connell Family, LLC, Artists First Management, LLC, Stardust Properties, LLC, Stardust Strategic Assets, LLC, Jessica Miller Center, LLC, and Aethelgard Holdings, LLC.

Mandatory Imprint Policy

Closed Submission Policy (No Unsolicited Demos)

Engine Room Records is a strictly closed private imprint dedicated exclusively to the creative works of Michael P. Ragsdale. We do not accept unsolicited demos, artist submissions, or representation inquiries. Any unsolicited submissions sent to our domain are automatically deleted at the mail transport layer before they ever arrive at an inbox.

Engine Room Records (Real-World Imprint)
